newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's Industrial Bank 96 profits lower.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's Industrial Bank 96 profits lower.

text.p: Industrial Development Bank said on Tuesday its 1996 net profits fell 39 percent to 2.94 million dinars ($4.2 million) attributed to sharply lower gains from its local stock portfolio.
Its 1996 pre-tax profits before allocations dropped 23 percent to 4.1 million dinars from 5.33 million dinars in 1995.
Assets of the bank dropped slightly in 1996 to 134.3 million dinars from 134.8 milllion dinars in 1996, the balance sheet showed.
The bank approved last year 168 medium and long term loans to the value of 42.4 million dinars against 143 loans worth a total 20.93 million dinars in 1995.
Outstanding loans at the end of 1996 stood at 110.70 dinars, a slight drop from from 101 million dinars in 1995 with more repayments than disbursements, the bank's annual report showed.

Bank officials say the bank is seeking a mixed credit facility of loans and risk capital from the European Investment Bank (EIB) to improve its financing ability. An EIB team will hold appraisal talks with the bank in June, they added.
The bank's record level net profits in 1995 of 4.8 million were mainly due to capital gains from sale of some of the banks local stock portfolio.
The bank's profits from its local stock portflio dropped sharply in 1996 to 41,649 dinars from 1.87 million dinars in 1995.
The bank will approve at its coming AGM distribution of 180 fils per share, unchanged from last 1995.

The bank, which provides low cost medium and long term loans to industrialists is 18 percent owned by the government, with over 50 percent of its capital held by Jordan's major banks and the rest by institutional and private investors.
Shareholders rights rose to 31 million dinars from 28 million dinars.
